nodes.label: Security Implementation Specification v3
nodes.rationale: Current and authoritative, at engineering level. Overrides convenience, speed and preference; where any document conflicts with it on a security matter, it wins.

nodes.label: Four Principles
nodes.rationale: Fail closed — a missing permission declaration is a denial. Never trust the client — role and scope are resolved server-side on every request. Authorize at the object, not the route: nearly every real-world data leak lives in the gap between confirming a caller is an administrator and confirming the requested record and operation are valid. Minimum exposure.

nodes.label: Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Curious or paid-off staff, external attacker after the membership list, opportunistic non-member after 30-40% discounts, dishonest staff recording redemptions that did not occur, and an insider bulk-extracting. Note the ordering: in version 1 the top threat was points fraud; here it is disclosure of who the members are and where they have been.

nodes.label: Argon2id Password Storage
nodes.rationale: m=65536, t=3, p=2, 16-byte unique random salt, 32-byte output; bcrypt at work factor 12 only if no maintained Argon2 binding exists. Algorithm and parameters stored alongside the hash so parameters can be raised and hashes upgraded transparently on next login. Constant-time comparison; minimum length rather than composition rules, screened against a breached-password list.

nodes.label: Password Pepper in a Key Management Service
nodes.rationale: Held in the KMS, not the database, so a stolen dump alone is not crackable. That non-colocation is the property the pepper exists for, and is the reason an environment variable is the nearest available substitute where no KMS exists.

nodes.label: Member Phone Plus One-Time Passcode
nodes.rationale: No passwords for members. Codes from a cryptographically secure source, stored hashed because a leaked table of live codes is account takeover, 5-minute TTL, single use, constant-time comparison, maximum 5 attempts, rate limited per number, per IP and globally to prevent SMS-pumping fraud.

nodes.label: Single-Use Claim Codes
nodes.rationale: Consumed atomically on first successful activation, at least 128 bits of entropy, never derived from the membership number which is printed on a card and sequential, stored hashed, expiring, bound to one member on issue, with strict rate limiting on the activation endpoint since a guessable claim code grants a genuine membership.

nodes.label: Uniform Responses and Timings
nodes.rationale: Login, activation and reset return identical responses and comparable timings whether or not the identifier exists. On a membership this exclusive, confirming that a given phone number belongs to a member is itself a disclosure.

nodes.label: Access Plus Opaque Refresh Token Architecture
nodes.rationale: A JWT cannot be individually revoked without building the server-side state it was meant to avoid, so the refresh token is opaque, hashed and carries a family ID. Access 10 min (panel) / 30 min (member app); refresh 12 hours (administrator) / 30 days sliding (member). Staff lifetimes are deliberately short: a member's session persisting is a convenience, a staff session persisting on a shared device is an exposure. Algorithm pinned server-side; iss and aud validated, not merely present.

nodes.label: Refresh Rotation with Family Reuse Detection
nodes.rationale: Every refresh issues a new token and invalidates the old one. If a spent token is presented again, revoke the whole family and force re-authentication — a legitimate client never replays one, so this turns a silent compromise into a detected one.

nodes.label: Token Version and Forced Re-Authentication
nodes.rationale: tv on the user record: incrementing it invalidates every outstanding access token — the mechanism behind logout-everywhere, role change and emergency revocation. Triggered by password change, role change, staff offboarding, membership suspension, suspected compromise and user-initiated logout-everywhere.

nodes.label: Client Token Storage Rules
nodes.rationale: httpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict refresh cookie for the panel and never localStorage, because any XSS flaw becomes total account theft. The access token stays in memory and state-changing routes use its bearer header. Keychain/Keystore on native. No tokens in URLs — they reach logs, history and referrer headers.

nodes.label: Deny by Default, Enforced at Boot
nodes.rationale: Every route declares its required permission and a route with no declaration fails application startup. The single highest-value control: the realistic failure is not a broken check but a new endpoint shipped under deadline with no check at all.

nodes.label: Scope the Query, Do Not Fetch Then Check
nodes.rationale: Loading a record before authorization is decided leaks its existence through errors, timing and logs. The query must be unable to return a record the caller may not see, and anything out of scope returns 404 rather than 403. Privilege elevation is verified server-side: a client-supplied approved:true is not an authorization decision. The document's own illustrative spread proved unsafe in practice.

nodes.label: Database Privilege Backstop
nodes.rationale: Even without competing tenants, defence in depth is worth the small cost: the application role holds no DELETE on members or redemptions and no UPDATE on redemptions. Destructive operations require a separate migration role.

nodes.label: Server-Side Metric and Dimension Allowlist
nodes.rationale: No client-supplied SQL ever, including fragments. Metrics and dimensions come from a server-side map of identifiers to validated expressions, and anything absent from the map is rejected before a query is built. Exports are a separate permission: administrator-only, rate-limited, individually audited and alerted.

nodes.label: Minimum Cohort Size of Five
nodes.rationale: The one threshold the specification states outright. Below it the endpoint returns 'insufficient data' rather than a number, because otherwise aggregate reporting becomes an indirect route to individual member movements — precisely what the document exists to protect.

nodes.label: API Hardening
nodes.rationale: Schema validation at the edge rejecting unknown fields rather than ignoring them, since mass-assignment flaws come from silently accepting extra keys. Parameterised queries only. Rate limiting by class, per IP and per principal. Exact-origin CORS allowlist, never a wildcard and never reflecting Origin. HSTS with preload, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, strict CSP without unsafe-inline. Certificate pinning in the member app. Pagination caps.

nodes.label: Logging Redaction and Append-Only Audit
nodes.rationale: Application logs contain no member names, phone numbers or email addresses — log the opaque reference only, enforced by a redaction layer on the logger rather than by convention. The audit log is separate, append-only and restricted, covering every record viewed, every lookup, export, benefit change, membership change, authentication event and authorization denial. Who viewed which member's history is itself sensitive information.

nodes.label: Data Protection Obligations
nodes.rationale: Consent captured per channel, unticked by default, stored with timestamp and wording version, withdrawable with immediate effect. Deletion honoured by irreversible anonymisation rather than row removal so aggregate reporting survives. A DPIA is required before launch. Hosting region decided before infrastructure is built. No special-category data: spa treatment records can imply health information, so record that a spa benefit was used, not what treatment was taken.

nodes.label: Authorization Matrix in CI
nodes.rationale: Administrator and member principals against every endpoint with declared expected outcomes; the build fails on any deviation, and retired database role values are tested as universal denials. Also automated: token manipulation, refresh reuse triggering family revocation, claim code reuse, small-cohort suppression and redemption idempotency under duplicate submission.

nodes.label: §12 Engineering Checklist
nodes.rationale: Thirty items across credentials, tokens, authorization and data. The checklist Stage 14's security review works through item by item, confirming each with a file reference or recording why it is deferred.
